title: How a Python loop works
topic: How does a Python loop work?
summary: This lesson explains how a standard Python for-loop operates over a sequence generated by range(3), showing step-by-step iteration and terminal output.
learning_objectives: Understand the basic syntax of a Python for-loop
Learn how the range() function generates numerical sequences
Trace variable assignment across consecutive loop iterations

key_concepts.definition: A control flow statement for specifying iteration along a sequence.
A built-in Python generator producing integers starting at 0 up to, but not including, n.
A single execution of the statements contained within the loop block.

step_by_step_explanation: The range(3) function generates the sequence [0, 1, 2].
Iteration 1: i takes value 0, print(0) executes.
Iteration 2: i takes value 1, print(1) executes.
Iteration 3: i takes value 2, print(2) executes.
The loop terminates when no more elements remain in the sequence.
key_takeaways: Loops prevent manual repetition of identical instructions.
The loop variable automatically advances on every pass.
range(3) produces 3 total iterations from 0 to 2.

revision_questions.question: What is the initial value of i when executing 'for i in range(3):'?
How many total iterations are executed by 'range(5)'?
